name: Biomechanics and Soft Robotics Lab
institution: Indian Institute of Technology Delhi
summary: The group studies soft and wearable robotics, computational design of morphology and body-integrated control; its parent center explicitly describes morphological computation in bio-inspired compliant robots.
activity: A 2026 IIT Delhi CoE-BIRD major project is attributed to the JATC Soft Robotics Lab and describes student work on an RL-controlled hip exoskeleton with simulation and hardware evaluation; the group roster lists current soft-robotics PhD work.

name: Biomedical System Engineering Lab — An-Chi Wei
institution: National Taiwan University, Department of Electrical Engineering; Graduate Institute of Biomedical Electronics and Bioinformatics
summary: The lab explicitly models how mitochondrial dynamics, energy supply and demand, and cellular coordination interact. It combines computational modelling and quantitative experiments, and its current 2025 publication uses a multiomics workflow and metabolic models to simulate cardiomyocyte perturbations. This is central work on cellular bioenergetics with a credible bridge to biological energy budgets and energy-aware computation. The bridge to energy consumption of AI/ML hardware is not claimed.

Current NTU Lab Spotlight and faculty pages identify Wei and her lab programme.

name: Biophysical Engineering of Life (Göpfrich Lab)
institution: Heidelberg University, ZMBH
summary: Group develops DNA/RNA encoding and processing, synthetic cells and molecular machinery; current 2025 RNA-origami work extends information-bearing machinery.
activity: Heidelberg’s March 2025 release reports a current advance and long-term work toward RNA-based synthetic-cell molecular machinery.

name: BioPhysics & Molecular Computing Group (Takinoue Lab)
institution: Institute of Science Tokyo
summary: Group studies chemical molecular computing and autonomous artificial-life-like systems through programmed nonequilibrium biomolecular reactions and synthetic cells.
activity: Current first-party page lists 2026 news and the group’s molecular computing, synthetic-cell and artificial-life research themes.

name: BioProgramming Lab — Zibo Chen
institution: School of Life Sciences, Westlake University
summary: The BioProgramming Lab builds programmable protein circuits and synthetic cells from minimal components to study biological organization and test what is required for life-like maintenance, replication and emergence from lifeless molecules. The origins and cellular computation themes are explicit in the current programme.
activity: Current Westlake profile identifies Chen as faculty and the BioProgramming Lab; the current lab people page lists an active group.

name: BISCUIT — Bio-Inspired Situated Cellular and Unconventional Information Technology
institution: LORIA-CNRS / University of Lorraine
summary: BISCUIT studies emergent properties of non-conventional neuro-cellular architectures, combining embodiment, unsupervised self-organization and distributed reinforcement learning for persistent autonomous agents implemented on neuromorphic hardware.
activity: Current official unit page was opened; the supplied October queue did not provide a dated activity item.

name: Blackiston Lab (Tufts University)
institution: Tufts University, Department of Biology; Visiting Scholar/Principal Investigator, Wyss Institute for Biologically Inspired Engineering at Harvard University
summary: The lab studies how stem-cell populations self-assemble into tissues and organisms and how developmental signaling can be used to control form, function, sensory-motor integration and regeneration. Its applied program engineers developing tissues as living materials for biosensors, biological robots and self-healing biohybrid devices. A 2025 organoid study analyzes information dynamics and functional connectivity in aneural tissue after injury.
activity: The first-party Tufts directory currently lists Blackiston as PI of The Blackiston Lab, and his lab page identifies him as Tufts Assistant Professor with a specific active research program. Blackiston coauthored the peer-reviewed paper “Revealing non-trivial information structures in aneural biological tissues via functional connectivity,” published 2025-04-14, examining calcium dynamics and network structure in Xenopus epidermal organoids before and after injury.

name: Boekhoven Lab — Systems Chemistry and Synthetic Life
institution: Technical University of Munich, TUM School of Natural Sciences, Department of Bioscience
summary: The lab builds synthetic cells and replicators from peptides, proteins and nucleic acids, using chemical fuels to produce competition, replication, mutation and selection. Recent work examines how genetic material changes protocell phenotype and behavior, making this a direct programme on synthetic living organization and the minimal properties of life.
activity: TUM’s July 2026 report documents a joint study showing DNA changes the stability and morphology of fuel-dependent coacervate protocells, a primitive genotype–phenotype coupling. The current TUM profile lists further 2026 synthetic-cell and autocatalysis work; the official lab home states its ongoing life-from-the-bottom-up aim.

name: BOLD Lab — British Open-Ended Learning and Discovery
institution: University of Oxford-led programme with University College London and Imperial College London
summary: BOLD is a current cross-university laboratory explicitly named for open-ended learning and discovery, a direct Bio-inspired theme 3 subject. Its current sources describe a national AI research programme with new learning methods, human-centric discovery, and embodied learning. Its Bio membership is a cross-track mapping question; the 2025 ASAL++ paper is not presented as a BOLD output.

name: Brain Energy Lab
institution: University of Sussex

activity: Official site identifies the active research group and current team/project pages.

name: BruBotics – Self-Healing Robotics Research Group
institution: Vrije Universiteit Brussel and imec
summary: The group develops materials and soft robots that sense damage, heal, restore function and assess repair. This row refers to its self-healing research, not all BruBotics labs.
activity: August 2026 VUB announcement documents current sensing/repair/adaptation work through RESSORT.

name: Cai Group — Neural Microsystems and In-Vitro Neural Computation
institution: Aerospace Information Research Institute, Chinese Academy of Sciences
summary: The current lab lead works on brain-interface microelectrode arrays and in-vitro neural computation. The 2026 AIRCAS report documents a current team demonstrating low-power, high-speed information processing by cultured biological neural networks.
activity: May 2026 AIRCAS research news reports the team’s low-power, high-speed neural-network computation publication.

name: Cancer Systems Biology Laboratory (Mohit Kumar Jolly)
institution: IISc, Department of Bioengineering
summary: Develops mechanistic models of cell-fate decision networks, cell-state heterogeneity, tissue patterning and collective migration. The 2025 work explicitly studies emergent cell decision dynamics in mutually repressive regulatory networks.
activity: Current lab page lists 2025 publication on emergent dynamics of cellular decision-making in regulatory networks; faculty profile and current lab roster confirm an active group.

name: Cell and Protein Engineering Laboratory — Laura Segatori
institution: Rice University, Departments of Bioengineering, Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering, and BioSciences
summary: The group designs feedback-controlled genetic circuits that sense molecular stress signals and dynamically alter endogenous cell-response pathways. The 2025 cell-factory paper couples intracellular sensing to circuit computation and active changes in cell fate/stress response, an explicit synthetic cellular-computation fit.
activity: Rice’s current faculty profile lists the active Segatori programme and ongoing funding; Rice currently lists Carlos Llanos as a graduate student linked to Segatori Lab. In May 2025, the group published a feedback-responsive cell factory paper: engineered circuits sense proteotoxic stress, dynamically modulate UPR pathways and increase production of tPA and blinatumomab. Segatori conceived the project and is corresponding author.

name: Cell Biophysics Lab (Bidisha Sinha)
institution: IISER Kolkata, Department of Biological Sciences
summary: Studies active regulation of plasma-membrane and actomyosin-cortex organization, mechanical heterogeneity, mechanosensing and endocytic trafficking. The cell-scale organization is explicit; its relation to Bio-inspired information processing is inferred.
activity: Current lab and research pages list current 2024–2026 research on cell volume regulation, cortex mechanics and membrane signaling; the 2026 symposium talk details actomyosin/endocytic regulation of membrane heterogeneity.

name: Cellular Computations and Learning Group
institution: Max Planck Institute for Neurobiology of Behavior — caesar
summary: The group explicitly develops theories and experiments for information processing and learning in single cells, including biochemical signal integration, memory, and response generalization. This directly matches the cellular/molecular computation and basal cognition themes.
activity: The 2026 KITP programme lists Koseska speaking on biological computations and learning without attractors; a 2024 peer-reviewed article is affiliated with the current lab and studies biological computation in signaling networks.

name: Cellular Learning, Adaptation & Control Group
institution: Technion — Israel Institute of Technology, Department of Chemical Engineering and Network Biology Research Laboratories
summary: The group explicitly studies learning, adaptation and control in brainless biological systems such as cells and cell populations, including exploratory dynamics in biological networks.

name: Centre of Excellence on Biologically Inspired Robots and Drones (CoE-BIRD)
institution: Indian Institute of Technology Delhi
summary: CoE-BIRD is a formally recognized interdisciplinary centre on biologically inspired robots and drones. name: Chair of Physics of Synthetic Biological Systems (Simmel Lab)
institution: Technical University of Munich, School of Natural Sciences, Department of Bioscience
summary: Current work explicitly aims to build self-organizing molecular/cellular systems that sense, compute, move and act; research includes DNA/RNA computing, cell-free synthetic cells, synthetic gene circuits, intercellular communication and programmed pattern formation. This is a direct molecular/cellular computation unit.
activity: The official members page lists Simmel as group leader and Bienau as a current PhD student; the publication page lists 2026 DNA molecular robotics and 2025–26 synthetic biology outputs.

name: Chair of Statistical Field Theory (CSFT), EPFL
institution: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)
summary: EPFL CSFT explicitly identifies artificial life, especially discrete and continuous cellular automata, as a key project area. Current postdoc Barbora Hudcová studies complex systems as ALife models, formal cellular-automata dynamics, self-replication and computational capacity; the group organized a 2026 ALIFE complexity workshop on cellular automata and emergent patterns. This is an explicit current artificial-life programme within a broader statistical field theory chair.
activity: Current CSFT page lists artificial life/cellular automata among key projects and a May 2026 workshop; the current roster lists Hudcová as postdoc. Her current research page and 2026 EPFL event details provide recent substantive activity.

name: Chao Zhong Laboratory — Materials Synthetic Biology
institution: Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences; Institute of Synthetic Biology / Materials Synthetic Biology Center
summary: The group builds programmable recombinase circuits that cause a founder cell to generate descendant populations at predicted, tunable ratios and with distinct functions. The current work explicitly frames cellular differentiation as computation and connects controlled lineage branching to multicellular organization and morphogenesis.
activity: Official March 2026 SIAT report and lab publication list document the jointly led Nature study: recombinase switches program cell fate branches and descendant ratios; a mathematical model predicts outcomes; engineered populations divide functional tasks. Current lab roster lists active PI, faculty and trainees.

name: Chemical Origins of Life Laboratory (COoL) — Sudha Rajamani
institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Pune
summary: The COoL lab studies how chemistry transitioned to biology through prebiotic polymers, self-assembly, replication and membranes that formed early cellular life. Current institutional page identifies Rajamani as professor and provides a substantive, mechanism-focused group programme.
activity: The institutional profile was updated 17 June 2026, identifies her current professorship and current COoL lab projects on protocell emergence, prebiotic chemistry and early Earth analogue sites.

name: Chemical Origins of Molecular Biology Group — John Sutherland
institution: MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology
summary: Sutherland’s current group page explicitly targets chemical origins of molecular biology through prebiotically plausible synthesis of information-bearing, catalytic and compartment-forming molecules, including RNA, translation, and lipids. Current group identity and 2025 activity are independently confirmed by MRC LMB.
activity: MRC LMB’s 2025 report identifies Sutherland as an active Group Leader and describes the continuing group’s work on prebiotic pathways and the chemical origins of cellular format, central dogma, and genetic code.

name: Cheng Zhang Group — DNA Molecular Circuits and Computing
institution: Peking University, School of Computer Science
summary: First-party lab scope explicitly includes complex DNA molecular circuit/computing; PKU profile documents 2026 peer-reviewed work.

name: Christopher Aaron O’Hara — Computational Disclosure / Autopoiesis Programme
institution: Independent researcher; Crossref paper affiliation: Global Center for Advanced Studies (GCAS)

summary: This current individual-led computational programme uses a self-modifying system to make organizational closure/autopoiesis assumptions explicit and testable. The ALIFE 2026 paper combines compositional graph reasoning for macro-action discovery with modal temporal logic verification and repeated-run stability analysis; a public code repository contains the executable model, DSL, metrics and validation helpers. The paper explicitly states this is not proof of life. It is therefore strongly related to grounded computational inquiry into living organization, not a claim of biological life, self-replication or experimentally validated autopoiesis.
activity: The Aug 2026 ALIFE paper and companion code are the active project; current author README says he is extending second-order cybernetics/modal logic to emergence and autopoiesis.

name: Chrystopher Nehaniv — artificial life and biological computation program
institution: University of Waterloo
summary: A current artificial-life and complex adaptive systems program includes automata, gene-regulatory networks, differentiated multicellularity, and cellular automata models of self-reproduction and evolution.
activity: Current full professor; co-organized the 2025 Distributed Ciphers session, whose stated scope includes biological computation, self-replication, morphogenesis and gene regulation.

name: Chunhai Fan Research Group — SJTU DNA Storage Research Center
institution: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Zhangjiang Advanced Research Institute
summary: The PI-led group has published molecular systems that implement general-purpose DNA computation and a DNA-framework state machine in living cells. The 2025 storage paper confirms current team activity, while the computational mechanisms identified are in 2023 work.

name: Claes Strannegård — ecosystem agent-modelling programme
institution: University of Gothenburg, Department of Applied IT, division CLIC
summary: An active PI-led computational ecosystem programme models plants, animals and abiotic environments. Its animal agents use homeostasis, learning and decision-making, with reinforcement learning or genetic algorithms to balance survival needs and reproduce predator-prey dynamics. The artificial-life/open-endedness fit is inferred from this mechanism evidence.
activity: NAISS-funded project Ecosystems, PI Claes Strannegård, started 2026-09-25 and runs to 2027-10-01. The project description specifies ecosystem modelling with homeostatic agents using reinforcement learning or genetic algorithms.

name: Cognitive Developmental Robotics Lab (Nagai Lab)
institution: The University of Tokyo, IRCN
summary: The lab uses computational and robotic methods to study cognitive development, including sensorimotor predictive learning and developmental mechanisms.
activity: Official lab sources list current 2026 papers and presentations.

name: Cognitive Neuroimaging Lab — Metabolic Connectivity Program
institution: Monash University
summary: The lab measures dynamic brain glucose metabolism and metabolic connectivity to understand cognition and aging; Jamadar coauthored the 2025 review on metabolic costs of cognition.

name: Collective Cellular Dynamics Laboratory (Tamal Das)
institution: Tata Institute of Fundamental Research Hyderabad
summary: The lab studies collective epithelial dynamics and tissue morphogenesis. Current mechanochemical work treats organelles as integrators of geometry, tension and biochemical signaling that control cell fate and leader emergence during wound healing and collective migration.
activity: The 2025 interview reports ongoing cell competition/morphogenesis work; the 2026 abstract for his current talk describes mechanochemical information processing and collective cell decisions; TIFR lists current research areas.

name: Collective Dynamics research group, University of Bristol
lead: Professor Jonathan Lawry; core team includes Chanelle Lee
institution: University of Bristol
summary: The current group studies system-level function emerging from interacting parts across biology, engineering and social science, with explicit modelling methods. The paper gives a direct computational self-organisation/neural cellular automata connection, without claiming biological morphogenesis or life.

The 2026 paper code repository documents the exact NeuralCA model and multi-agent mapping experiments; current official Bristol pages list recent 2026 research activity by group members.

name: Complex Adaptive System Laboratory (Takadama Lab)
institution: The University of Tokyo, Graduate School of Information Science and Technology
summary: Takadama's group explicitly derives open-ended learning and continuously growing AI from biological evolution and developmental processes, generating new tasks, morphologies, and strategies rather than only solving predefined problems.
activity: Presentations at the Evolutionary Computation Symposium 2025 and a JSAI journal interview with Prof. Takadama; lab page copyright 2026.

name: Complex Adaptive Systems and Computational Intelligence (CASCI) research group
institution: Binghamton University, School of Systems Science and Industrial Engineering; Católica Biomedical Research Center collaboration
summary: CASCI has an active, explicitly named research programme developing canalization and schema-redescription methods for automata networks used to model gene regulation and biochemical signalling. The group links network redundancy to cellular activity, causal control, dynamical modularity and collective computation in intracellular systems. This is a computational methods programme for cellular/molecular systems, rather than generic complex-systems research. name: Complex Quantum Systems
institution: University of Maryland, Baltimore County
summary: Studies computational resources in physical dynamics and the foundations of statistical mechanics. Natural computation is an explicit research theme.

name: Complex Systems Lab (Ricard Solé)
institution: Institute of Evolutionary Biology (IBE), Spanish National Research Council (CSIC) and Pompeu Fabra University (UPF); ICREA
summary: The Complex Systems Lab studies evolutionary origins of complex systems through mathematical models and synthetic-biology experiments, including protocells, cognition, cellular circuits and artificial systems in silico. Ricard Solé coauthored Eco-Evo-Devox, a modular artificial-life platform that makes ecology, development and embodied neural evolution jointly manipulable. This direct current paper link supports an inferred bridge from the lab’s broader synthetic and artificial-systems programme to Bio-inspired developmental and neural-evolution research; it does not establish a separately named neural-evolution subunit.
activity: Ricard Solé coauthored the 2025 ALIFE proceedings paper describing Eco-Evo-Devox, an artificial-life platform for ecological and developmental roots of neural evolution. The current IBE lab page names him PI and lists ongoing synthetic-ecosystem work, current lab members and 2026 publications; the lab remit explicitly includes artificial systems and cognition.

name: Complexity and Astrobiology Group — Jacobo Aguirre
institution: Centro de Astrobiología (CAB, CSIC-INTA), Molecular Evolution Department
summary: This named research group applies mathematical and computational models, complexity theory and network science to the origin and early evolution of life, including whether diversity, inheritance and replication can emerge naturally from simple models.

The linked external group page returned 404 in this check, so no current member roster is claimed.

name: Computational Cell Biology (Mukund Thattai)
institution: National Centre for Biological Sciences, TIFR
summary: Uses quantitative models and cell biology to study how molecular interactions and vesicle traffic organize intracellular systems and regulate distributed biochemical activity; the cell is explicitly framed as a logical/computational machine.

name: Computational Cell Fate
institution: Radboud Institute for Molecular Life Sciences, Radboud University
summary: The group models how individual cells process cell-cell and environmental signals, communicate across scales and make robust fate decisions, using mechanistic biophysics and single-cell data. This is a specific cellular information-processing bridge; its computational approach does not by itself define the relevance.
activity: The first-party group page reports an August 2026 Cell Systems paper on heterogeneous cell-cell communication and September 2026 group hires; its current group roster and methods page corroborate ongoing programme.

name: Computational Immunology Group (Radboud University / Radboudumc)
institution: Radboud University, Institute for Computing and Information Sciences, and Radboud University Medical Center, Department of Medical BioSciences
summary: The group explicitly studies how adaptive immune cells process information, learn and collaborate to make collective decisions. Current projects combine AI, biophysical simulations and immune-cell data to decode immune responses, and the Artificial Immunological Intelligence programme uses immune-system learning to inform both immunology and machine learning. This directly fits cellular/basal cognition and collective-cell intelligence; no broader ordinary immunology inference is needed.
activity: Current official project pages include “AI and Simulations for Decoding the Spatiotemporal Dynamics of Immune Responses” (2023–2028) and “Artificial Immunological Intelligence” (2020–2026). The group’s publication list includes 2025 GECCO output and 2026 T-cell immunology and collective-behaviour papers; its current roster names Textor (Associate Professor) and Wortel (Assistant Professor).

name: Computational Intelligence Group
institution: Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, Department of Computer Science
summary: The active group develops systems that self-organize, evolve, and learn, including evolutionary computing and robotics; the 2025 robot-fertility paper directly extends evolved robot populations.
activity: Current group roster/vision and current 2025 GECCO output identify the active evolutionary-robotics program.

name: Computational Magnetic Metamaterials (COMET)
institution: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU), Faculty of Information Technology and Electrical Engineering; cross-department Computer Science and Electronic Systems researchers
summary: COMET investigates artificial life and unconventional computation in physical materials, especially artificial spin ice. Its current nanomagnetic work uses evolutionary algorithms to discover life-like patterns in a material substrate, including gliders and interacting “creatures,” and studies their computation and low-power computing potential. This directly fits the Bio-inspired in-materio/physical computation and artificial-life boundary without asserting biological motivation.

summary: The lab’s funded research includes DNA computing systems and algorithms for large-scale artificial neural networks and DNA memory software/hardware, rather than DNA merely as a data label.

summary: The current lab describes its programme as nature-inspired computing, investigates emergent memory and hierarchy in digital evolution for dynamic partially observable predictive control, and includes current evolutionary-robotics and neurobiologically inspired AI projects. summary: Current Rojas-supervised work includes a CRISPR-Cas12a dengue-detection system and DNA-aptamer detection projects, alongside his molecular/synthetic-biology research programme. institution: Complexity Sciences Center, University of California, Davis
summary: Develops computational mechanics, learning dynamics, evolving cellular automata and physical information engines. Current momentum-computing work addresses energy, speed and fidelity constraints.

institution: University of Konstanz, Department of Computer and Information Science
summary: Current group work includes evolutionary robotics, swarm robotics, bio-hybrid systems and robot-plant systems. This maps directly to evolutionary robotics and body–brain co-design.

summary: The lab investigates post-transcriptional regulatory networks, cell-state transitions and cell-fate decisions in planarian regeneration and embryonic-stem-cell differentiation. activity: The CCG profile lists 2025 peer-reviewed activity on CRISPR/Cas transposition-system regulation in native V. parahaemolyticus. The 2023 OpaR paper is a specific mechanism/activity item showing dynamic c-di-GMP homeostasis and downstream biofilm gene regulation; CCG currently describes decision-making/signal-processing as the lab remit.

name: Deans Lab
institution: Georgia Institute of Technology
summary: The group engineers genetic circuits to impose temporal and logical control over stem-cell differentiation and to create cells that sense and respond to disease; its stated work uses ML to identify cell-fate decision points.
activity: Current lab roster lists active students and ongoing research; 2025 lab publications in cell engineering and circuit design are listed in current team material.

name: Decisions, Feedback and Games in Biological Systems (Sandeep Krishna)
institution: National Centre for Biological Sciences, TIFR
summary: Models computation, feedback and decision-making in active cellular processes, chemical reaction networks and cooperative cell populations.
activity: The 2024 study by Sandeep Krishna and collaborators analyzes relaxation dynamics in chemical reaction networks and relates reaction-network topology to cellular network behavior; official NCBS profile lists ongoing computation using active cellular processes.

name: Developmental Epigenetics
institution: Radboud Institute for Molecular Life Sciences, Radboud University
summary: The group investigates cellular patterning, symmetry breaking, embryo development and cell-fate decisions using gastruloids, blastoids and stem-cell models. These are direct morphogenesis and developmental mechanisms.
activity: The institutional group page lists active grants through 2028/29, 2025 publications and a current multi-person team; its research lines explicitly include patterning, symmetry breaking and cellular interactions.

name: DeWeese Lab
institution: University of California, Berkeley
summary: Combines nonequilibrium molecular-machine control, first-principles neural-network theory and biologically plausible neural computation.
activity: Current lab roster lists D’Ambrosia as a graduate student; his August 2026 talk studies finite-precision computation and thermodynamic cost. The lab’s current site states active research across stat mech, learning and neuroscience.

name: Dibyendu Das research group — non-equilibrium self-assembly
institution: Indian Institute of Science Education and Research Kolkata
summary: Current group studies dissipative molecular assemblies and integration of life-like properties.
activity: Official lab/publication list shows 2025 papers on autopoietic vesicles and dissipative assemblies.

name: Dieter Braun Research Group — Biophysics of Evolution
institution: Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München, Faculty of Physics
summary: The group experimentally studies how physical non-equilibrium settings such as heated rock cracks and gas-liquid interfaces drive accumulation, replication, selection and autonomous molecular evolution. Its work directly tests mechanisms connecting prebiotic chemistry to living systems.
activity: The current group site names a 2025–2031 ERC Synergy award with Hannes Mutschler and lists multiple 2024–25 papers on protocell formation, RNA replication, prebiotic polymerization and chemical evolution.

name: Digital Chemistry Group — Cronin Group
institution: School of Chemistry, University of Glasgow

Its 2026 reports include an experimental chemical-reaction-network assembly measure relevant to emergence and a molecular-replication/droplet-growth result. The same group is already recorded in the AI-for-Science track for chemical automation; this row adds Bio membership only.
activity: Maintained group site reports dated 2026 work on chemical reaction network directedness, molecular replication, droplets, and chemical artificial-life research.

name: Digital Evolution Laboratory
institution: Michigan State University

name: Distributed Intelligence / Autonomous Learning Group
institution: University of Tübingen

name: Distributed Intelligence and Optimization Lab (Giovanni Iacca)
institution: University of Trento, Department of Information Engineering and Computer Science
summary: The lab’s 2026 QD/Hebbian paper evolves diverse policies with local neuron-centric plasticity on RL tasks; its 2025 work applies QD to co-design soft-robot morphology and control. The underlying program is evolutionary and biologically inspired computation rather than biology-only data science.
activity: 2026 University of Trento conference/proceedings activity and current self-reported Associate Professor role; repository lists two 2026 evo-computation papers.

name: Diya Binoy Joseph Lab — Programming and Patterning of Epithelial Barriers
institution: Institute for Stem Cell Science and Regenerative Medicine (inStem)
summary: The lab studies how developmental cues pattern regionally specialized epithelial identity and organize immune-cell niches along tissue axes, using organotypic systems, spatial/single-cell methods and organoids. The exact biological patterning mechanism is explicit; its relevance to engineered or computational systems is inferred.
activity: Her inStem PI page reports corresponding-author papers in Developmental Biology (April 2025) and Mucosal Immunology (September 2025), a 2026 urethral-organoid methods publication, and an independent laboratory active since 2022.

name: DNA and Natural Algorithms Group (Caltech)
institution: California Institute of Technology
summary: Group studies biomolecular computation, DNA circuits, molecular programming, self-assembly and molecular robots.
activity: DNA32 2026 volume includes a Winfree coauthored paper; official proceedings author affiliation and group page support current unit attribution.

name: Dobata Lab
institution: The University of Tokyo, Graduate School of Arts and Sciences
summary: The current lab studies insect social and collective systems through empirical work, mathematical/computational analysis and simulation. Its current PI explicitly collaborates with engineers on ant-inspired swarm systems and uses robots as synthetic models to study how collective behavior emerges. This provides a direct biological-mechanism to engineered-swarm bridge that fits the Bio-inspired scope. The water-beetle paper is a concrete current collective-autonomy study; the fit does not depend on claiming that beetles are cells or on generalizing all ecology into AI.
activity: Official publications page updated 2026-09-21 lists current 2026 insect collective papers and the 2025 ALIFE water-beetle study. The lab’s current 2025 reports include ongoing behavior tracking and collective-behavior work; official faculty page confirms PI role and active swarm-robotics collaboration.

name: Donald H. Burke-Agüero Lab — RNA catalysis and origins of life
institution: University of Missouri, Bond Life Sciences Center
summary: The lab studies relationships among RNA sequence, function, selection, design, and evolution, including catalytic mechanisms relevant to early life.
activity: The current ©2026 Bond LSC page identifies Burke-Agüero as PI and describes active lab themes; it explicitly states development of robust multiple-turnover ribozyme catalysts for engineered metabolism, synthetic biology, and origins-of-life applications.

name: Dongrui Liu — Trustworthy AI / agent-evolution programme
institution: Shanghai AI Laboratory
summary: Current research-scientist programme leads and corresponds on named harness-policy co-evolution and self-evolving LLM-agent work.

name: Doron Lancet Lab — Systems Biology and Protobiology
institution: Weizmann Institute of Science, Department of Molecular Genetics
summary: The lab models early living organization as self-reproducing catalytic lipid assemblies. Its GARD work examines growth and fission, compositional inheritance, self-reproduction, selection and the transition from chemical to biological evolution.
activity: The first-party publication list includes 2024 work on GARD prebiotic reproduction and order/complexity and 2026 work integrating composome and RNA-replicase origin models; the current lab page was updated in July 2026 and its group-members page in September 2026.

name: Droplet Laboratory — Jitka Čejková group
institution: Department of Chemical Engineering, University of Chemistry and Technology Prague (UCT Prague)
summary: A current wet artificial-life group studies droplets as liquid robots and self-organizing chemical systems, including chemotactic and collective droplet behavior, life-like shape change, and cell encapsulation for microbial communication. activity: The lab homepage lists 2026 events and research activity, identifies Čejková as lab lead, describes the group as a wet artificial-life lab, and reports that it accepts students. Its research page describes current study of droplet chemotaxis/collective behavior, chemical gardens and cell encapsulation for microbial communication.

name: Duke DNA and Molecular Computing Program
institution: Duke University
summary: Duke’s official program describes DNA/RNA molecular-scale computation. The current Reif lab record lists active molecular-scale AI work and recent DNA-circuit papers; Nagipogu, a coauthor of the 2023 review, is listed as a current student.
activity: The 2026-updated lab page lists current Molecular Assembly and Computation teaching and a current molecular-scale-AI graduate project; Duke ECE lists 2025 neural chemical-reaction-network learning and 2024 DNA computation papers.

name: Dynamic Protocellular Systems — Dora Tang Lab
institution: Saarland University
summary: Tang’s current Saarland programme builds synthetic-cell and protocellular systems from molecular compartments and reactions. Its 2026 study of self-organizing artificial droplets that protect genetic material and regulate biochemical reactions directly investigates mechanisms of living-like organization and is relevant to the origins of cellular life.
activity: Saarland University’s 2026 news report documents Tang-led work on artificial molecular droplets that self-organize, protect genetic material, and regulate biochemical reactions.

name: Dynamical Systems Biology Lab — Jordi Garcia-Ojalvo
institution: Universitat Pompeu Fabra, Department of Medicine and Life Sciences (MELIS)
summary: The current lab explicitly links dynamical living systems to natural computation, information processing and learning. Its single-cell learning programme and CeLEARN work provide a direct mechanism-level fit to cellular/molecular computation and basal biological learning.

institution: Institute of Science Tokyo

name: ECSO Lab — evolutionary cell physiology and origins of cellular complexity
institution: Purdue University
summary: The lab studies origins of eukaryotes and mitochondria, symbioses, and physiological/energetic constraints on cell evolution using large-scale phylogenetics, comparative genomics, bioinformatics, metagenomics, cultivation, and mathematical modeling.
activity: Purdue’s current faculty page lists the assistant professor and 2024 work on energetic costs of cellular complexity; it describes an active research program on origins of major cell innovations and transitions.

name: Eidosoma — Living Intelligence Research Lab
institution: Eidosoma
summary: Eidosoma is an explicitly identified current research lab directed by founder Robert Bjarnason. Its 2026 computational programme investigates how compositional inheritance can break, renew and be actively maintained in an origin-of-life GARD model, then tests related inheritance dynamics in cellular automata and gene-regulatory networks. Its current announced programme also addresses protocells, artificial life and distributed cell cognition. This is grounded life-organization and computational research; simulations are not evidence that autonomous life or a universal origin mechanism has been produced.
activity: Founder-authored preprint/blog dated 2026-09-12 reports computational experiments using GARD, cellular automata and Wagner gene-regulatory networks to test inheritance break/renewal and interventions; public research record details reconstructions and limits. The official team page says Eidosoma was established in 2026 and names Bjarnason as founder.

name: Eiko Matsuda — Human Harmony Design Science and Engineering programme
institution: Keio University, Faculty of Science and Technology, Department of System Design Engineering
summary: The current Keio researcher programme explicitly lists artificial life and embodied cognitive science and studies pre-representational sense-making, learning and human cognition, with findings embodied in AI, robots, VR and games. Recent ALIFE and 2025–2026 work make this an evidenced artificial-life/cognition programme; its connection to open-endedness is an inferred mechanism bridge.
activity: Keio researcher page, updated 2026-08-07, lists current programme and 2025/2026 papers on pre-representational dynamic sense-making and embodied cognition; official faculty page confirms current assistant-professor appointment.

name: Elias Barriga Group
institution: TU Dresden, Cluster of Excellence Physics of Life
summary: Studies the biophysical mechanisms by which endogenous electric and mechanical signals coordinate collective cell migration/differentiation, tissue morphogenesis, embryogenesis and regeneration. The computational relevance is an explicit inferred bridge from multi-cellular coordination and control, not a claim that the group builds AI.
activity: The group roster identifies Barriga as current group leader and lists active trainees/postdocs; the 2026 HFSP award funds electrochemical actuation of tissue morphogenesis. The team includes Nunes, who is therefore covered here.

name: Elisa Biondi PI programme at FfAME
institution: Foundation for Applied Molecular Evolution, with joint appointment at Firebird Biomolecular Sciences
summary: Biondi’s current PI programme studies prebiotic formation and evolution of informational molecules, RNA formation on mineral/geological surfaces and the evolutionary capacity of expanded genetic alphabets.
activity: The current first-party PI profile says Biondi is PI/Fellow (2012–present), lists active projects on prebiotic informational molecules, and lists 2025 AEGIS replication and PNAS prebiotic RNA synthesis work. Current team directory labels her Principal Investigator & Fellow.

name: Elisha Moses Lab — Physics of Biological Computation
institution: Weizmann Institute of Science, Department of Physics of Complex Systems
summary: The lab explicitly investigates biological computation at the protein and enzyme scale and describes enzymes as programmable viscoelastic materials. Its 2025 enzyme-mechanics study is a current mechanistic contribution to this programme.
activity: The first-party publication list records the lab lead as coauthor on “Enzymes as viscoelastic catalytic machines,” Nature Physics 21(5), 787–798 (2025), and gives its mechanistic abstract. The same page also records a 2025 PNAS paper, though that speech-prosody work is not used to establish Bio fit.

name: ELIXIR Lab
institution: Toronto Metropolitan University
summary: ELIXIR explicitly studies embodied damage recovery in reconfigurable robotics and bio-inspired shape-morphing soft robotics.
activity: Current official portfolio lists active work on damage recovery and bio-inspired shape morphing.

name: Elowitz Lab — Synthetic and Systems Biology
institution: California Institute of Technology, Division of Biology and Biological Engineering
summary: The current lab combines synthetic molecular-circuit construction with single-cell analysis to understand and program cellular sensing, response, memory, and cell-fate behaviors. Current 2026 outputs include engineered cell-decision mechanisms.
activity: The lab-maintained publication page lists 2026 work on engineered caspase control and combinatorial integration of dopamine receptor signals. The official 2026 KITP schedule lists an Elowitz talk on synthetic circuits for programmable recognition and targeting.

name: Embodied Cognitive Science Unit (ECSU)
institution: Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology (OIST)
summary: ECSU conducts current research spanning origins of life and self-optimization, and explicitly uses computational modelling and artificial-life approaches. Current unit member Georgii Karelin studies artificial life/astrobiology, self-organization and enclosed ecosystem adaptation using nonlinear dynamics, cellular automata and agent-based models. This is relevant foundational modelling of life-like organization and adaptive living systems, but the unit is broadly embodied cognitive science and does not present itself as a dedicated biological-computation lab; relevance is therefore strongly related rather than core.
activity: Current unit pages describe origins-of-life and self-optimization research using artificial life and computational models; the current team roster identifies Karelin as a doctoral candidate working on artificial life, astrobiology, self-organization and ecosystem adaptation. The unit publications page lists current 2026 outputs, including work coauthored by Froese and Karelin.

name: Embrapa Synthetic Biology Laboratory (LBS)
institution: Embrapa Genetic Resources and Biotechnology
summary: Current LBS remit includes CRISPR- and synthetic-RNA-based biosensors, cell-free synthetic protein systems and synthetic-cell research. The bridge to molecular computation is inferred from molecular sensing and information processing; the current first-party programme does not claim logic gates or explicit computation.
activity: Embrapa bibliography records the 2025 ACS Synthetic Biology article “Cell-free production of soybean leghemoglobins and nonsymbiotic hemoglobin” by current LBS researchers including Bittencourt and Rech. Current LBS and researcher pages identify the active unit and its biosensor/synthetic-cell remit.

name: Emergence and Control in Development and Evolution (Archishman Raju)
institution: National Centre for Biological Sciences, TIFR
summary: Develops compact mathematical models of morphogenetic fields, Waddington landscapes, Turing patterns and developmental dynamics, including how development changes evolutionary trajectories.
activity: NCBS 2024–25 annual report lists the lab's 2025 preprint on a Waddingtonian model of Turing-pattern dynamics and current work on developmental trajectories; current faculty page identifies the ongoing group program.

name: EMERGENCE@ASU — Sara Imari Walker Lab
institution: Arizona State University, Beyond Center for Fundamental Concepts in Science
topics: emergence of life from nonliving matter
summary: The group develops theory and experiments to understand what life is and how life emerges from nonliving matter, including assembly theory as a measurable treatment of complexity, selection, and molecular organization. The current team page identifies Walker and active team members. This is an active origins-of-life mechanism programme, separate in identity from the broader Beyond Center.
activity: The maintained lab homepage and team page currently describe the research programme and identify Walker as professor and team lead; the research page gives active work on assembly theory and origin-of-life transition mechanisms.

name: Emerging Intelligent Substrates (EIS) Lab
institution: Institute of Neuroinformatics, University of Zurich / ETH Zurich
topics: morphogenesis/self-organisation, neural cellular automata and repair
summary: The EIS group’s current first-party remit explicitly investigates how intelligence emerges from physical substrates, studies brain structure-function across spatial/temporal scales, and uses silicon/resistive-memory devices to build intelligent systems. This is a specific biological/computational bridge in efficient physical computation and substrate-aware self-organization; it is not being counted because Gabriel Béna coauthored the paper alone. The current roster establishes him as a postdoc in Payvand’s group, while the lab itself has its own identity and programme. The ALIFE digital-circuit paper is not claimed as an EIS output.
activity: Official current UZH/ETH roster lists Gabriel Béna as a postdoc in Payvand’s group; his current 2026 CV describes ongoing research in memristive substrates and modular computation. The official EIS page describes active group projects and methods.

institution: Boğaziçi University
summary: Uğur’s current program models developmental progress in robot sensorimotor learning and goal understanding. The source describes formation of a developmental-robotics group; this is recorded as a research programme, not a formal lab brand.
activity: Current project page gives a 2025–2027 program; official profile confirms his present faculty role.

name: Endothelial Cell Biology and Vascular Regeneration (Soumyashree Das)
institution: National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS-TIFR)
summary: The programme studies the cell and molecular mechanisms of vascular growth and remodeling, including developmental arterial patterning and tissue repair through vascular regeneration. It directly fits morphogenesis and repair.

name: Engineered and Experimental Evolution (E3) Lab
institution: University of Michigan, Department of Ecology and Evolutionary Biology; Center for the Study of Complex Systems
summary: The E3 Lab studies biological evolutionary mechanisms through paired computational and microbial experimental systems. Its current programme models host–parasite coevolution with populations of self-replicating digital organisms and investigates microbial host–virus evolution, directly connecting artificial life to biological evolution.

A March 18, 2026 UMich MIDAS article documents Moreno’s active agent-based biological-evolution and lineage-tracking programme under Zaman and Dolson; UMich’s current CSCS directory lists Moreno in Zaman E3 Lab.

name: Ennis Research Group – Solid-State Astrochemistry and Molecular Crystal Spectroscopy
institution: University of Otago, Department of Chemistry
summary: Laboratory astrochemistry examines molecular reactions and amino-acid precursor pathways in Titan-relevant ice/clathrate systems; the university explicitly frames the programme as investigating pathways toward life’s building blocks and Titan’s origin-of-life chemistry.
activity: Current group site posted June 2026; Otago profile lists 2026 Titan-related papers; group carries ongoing Titan co-crystal research beyond the 2022–2024 Marsden award period.

name: Epigenomics and Single Cell Biophysics Group
institution: Radboud Institute for Molecular Life Sciences, Radboud University
summary: The group studies specific epigenetic and metabolic mechanisms that let innate immune cells retain prior-stimulus history and alter later responses. Persistent lncRNA, chromatin and histone-lactylation states form a molecular cellular-memory mechanism, which is relevant by inference to basal cellular computation and learning. The connection is mechanistic and non-neural; the group does not claim to build AI or a computational device.

summary: ELSI currently lists him as a specially appointed professor; current first-party research evidence documents a computational chemical-evolution project and 2026 enzyme-evolution collaboration, addressing emergence and organization of life.
activity: Current ELSI roster and SFI profile identify his roles/programme; dated Dec 2024 and Sep 2026 ELSI primary reports document computational chemistry and early metabolism work.

institution: European Molecular Biology Laboratory (EMBL)
summary: Combines soft-matter and non-equilibrium physics with nonlinear dynamics to study how molecular signaling, cell mechanics and geometry generate self-organisation and embryo morphogenesis.

summary: EvoChromo is a new decentralized lab asking when and how chromatin arose from prokaryotic building blocks and how its innovation contributed to cellular diversification and complex multicellular life. name: OPUS Lab — Orchestrating Physics for Unconventional Systems

name: Pablo Martín Gleiser — connectome-driven interacting-robot programme
institution: Instituto Tecnológico de Buenos Aires (ITBA), Department of Research and Doctorate
summary: The current ITBA project explicitly studies emergent behaviour in interacting robots. The robot's controller instantiates the C. elegans connectome, with sensor inputs activating sensory neurons and motor-neuron outputs controlling movement. name: Paradigms of Intelligence (Pi), Google Research
institution: Google Research
summary: Pi studies how life and intelligence emerge and evolve through natural computing. Its computational-life work investigates spontaneous self-replication in interacting programs; 2026 studies examine replication, cooperation and the physical costs of computation. The team also develops neural cellular automata and other approaches to self-organising computation.

name: Pashine Lab — trainable mechanical metamaterials and physical memory
institution: Syracuse University, Department of Physics
summary: The lab develops trainable mechanical materials that store and retrieve mechanical history and can be designed through training. This is directly relevant to the physical-learning part of theme 4; sources do not claim a biological system or measured energy efficiency.
activity: The current group publication page records 2025 work on adaptive force chains and reconfigurable granular metamaterials, plus a 2026 preprint on learning associations in particle packings. A current group roster identifies Pashine as PI and lists an active team. The official RRI seminar in May 2026 describes mechanical memory as usable for computation and self-organization.

name: Pasquale Stano Research Group
institution: University of Salento, Department of Biological and Environmental Sciences and Technologies
summary: Current group research explicitly spans origins of life, synthetic biology, systems chemistry and artificial life, with current wetware-AI and bottom-up synthetic-cell work.

name: Paul Higgs — Theoretical RNA-World and Protocell Programme
institution: McMaster University, Department of Physics & Astronomy
summary: Higgs’s current research programme combines theoretical and computational biophysics with mechanistic models of RNA replication, autocatalytic metabolism and protocell organization. Recent work tests how RNA templating can maintain reaction activity within protocells and how autocatalysis can drive vesicle growth and division.
activity: The 2025 Physical Review E paper (published 2025-01-31) models second-order autocatalysis that supports a stable active state inside a protocell while the environment remains unreactive, and connects nonenzymatic RNA templating to replication–metabolism coupling. A separate 2025 paper models protocell growth and division driven by autocatalysis.

name: Pei-Ying Lin — open-ended textile computation and cellular-automata researcher programme
institution: Independent artist-researcher practice; 2026 project commissioned by the Museum of Fiber Arts, Taichung
summary: Lin’s 2026 researcher-led textile-computation programme applies cellular-automata rules iteratively to weaving structures and examines emergent outcomes shaped by rule variation, material behaviour, machine constraints and human intervention. The programme explicitly frames this as open-ended computation and computational creativity, directly matching the open-endedness theme. It makes no claim of biological inspiration or cellular computation.

name: Pervasive Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (PAILab)

name: PhABLE Group — Physics of Adaptation, Learning and Evolution in Biology
institution: Yale University, Department of Immunobiology and Biomedical Engineering; Yale Center for Systems and Engineering Immunology
summary: PhABLE explicitly studies biological learning, adaptation and evolution of molecular programs through the immune system. activity: Yale profile updated January 2026 explicitly lists ongoing projects and 2024–2026 research outputs, including T-cell memory decision, adaptive response design, immune receptor variability and somatic evolution. The current PhABLE site details the research direction.

institution: University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, Department of Information and Computer Sciences; Department of Physics and Astronomy

activity: Current group page lists 2026 tissue and active-matter publications and identifies its dual Barcelona/Dresden base and funding; official Max Planck report independently lists the PI-led biological-physics group.

name: PHYSIX — computational prebiotic chemistry programme

name: Quantitative Cell Biology Lab (Shaon Chakrabarti)

activity: A 2025 iScience paper models circadian control of cell proliferation using stochastic simulations and single-cell lineage data; current NCBS PI page and research page describe the active lab programme and recruitment.

name: Rafael Peña Miller Programme — bacterial adaptation and cellular phenotypic heterogeneity
institution: Centro de Ciencias Genómicas, Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México (UNAM), Systems Biology Program

institution: Indiana University Bloomington, Cognitive Science Program; Program in Neuroscience; Luddy School of Informatics, Computing, and Engineering

name: Reena Singh Lab — Cardiovascular Development and 3D Organoid Morphogenesis

summary: The group studies how cell plasticity and adaptation let zebrafish liver/pancreas tissues recover from injury and metabolic stress, with single-cell, live-imaging and gene-editing methods. This directly addresses biological tissue repair and regeneration.

name: Research Group on Epistemology of the Sciences of the Artificial (RG-ESA) — Synthetic Biology and Embodied AI
institution: IULM University; University of Bologna; University of Salento
summary: The current RG-ESA lead coauthored a 2025 framework for chemical-network cognition and protocellular agents; an official 2023–26 collaborative project specifies wetware models of minimal biological cognition and synthetic-biology methods.
activity: RG-ESA is coordinated by Damiano; the collaborative SB-EAI effort includes Roli and Stano, with 2025 publications. Named 2023–26 project ended February 2026; the wider group is retained based on ongoing faculty roles and 2025–26 publication activity.

researchPlans.title: Org(SB-EAI) - An Organizational Approach to the Synthetic Modeling of Cognition based on Synthetic Biology and Embodied AI
researchPlans.author: Luisa Damiano

name: Richard Löffler — active-matter and complex chemical systems research programme
institution: Globe Institute and Centre for Star and Planet Formation, University of Copenhagen
summary: A current independent-PI programme studies active matter and complex chemical systems as models for life and its origin. Recent work and 2026 experiments examine chemical self-propulsion, dissipative droplet behavior and collective dynamics resembling chemotaxis or swarming. The fit is mechanistic and relevant to basal agency and self-organization, but sources do not establish an engineered artificial-life or computational device, so it remains STRONGLY_RELATED.
activity: The University of Copenhagen profile identifies Löffler as an independent PI studying active matter/complex chemical systems and life origins. A 2026 NBI seminar details ongoing lab experiments with self-propelled droplets and primitive agency. His peer-reviewed 2024 paper analyzes aggregation of self-propelled rods.

name: Rita Mateus Group
institution: TU Dresden, Cluster of Excellence Physics of Life (PoL), Dresden
summary: The group directly investigates how electrical, chemical, and mechanical signals encode information for proportional organ growth and regeneration.
activity: Official 2026 news reports current Science Advances work on injury-induced electrochemical coupling, organ growth, and repair; current group page lists active members.

name: Robert M. Hazen's Origins of Life research group
institution: Carnegie Institution for Science, Earth & Planets Laboratory
summary: Hazen’s current group studies prebiotic chemistry in mineral, ocean and atmospheric contexts and constrains plausible origin-of-life pathways through geochemistry. Carnegie’s 2025 work examines molecular signatures of ancient life in rocks, showing current activity.
activity: Carnegie’s 2025 report names Hazen on a current study applying chemical analysis and machine learning to more than 400 samples, including ancient rocks, fossils, meteorites and living organisms, to detect preserved signatures of life.

name: Robinson Group
institution: Institute for Molecules and Materials, Radboud University
summary: The group studies self-organizing chemical reaction networks as information-processing systems, including chemical reservoir computation and prebiotic reaction networks. Official research pages state the biological inspiration and list current information-processing mechanisms.
activity: The publications page lists Robinson’s 2026 article on information in chemical reaction systems, 2025 prebiotic-network work and the 2024 reservoir-computation paper; group members page lists current PhD and postdoctoral members.

name: ROBIOLAB — Bioinspired Robotics Laboratory
institution: Universidad de los Andes, Department of Mechanical Engineering
summary: Current ROBIOLAB projects include a parameterized automated search over gripper morphologies, with simulation screening of hundreds of geometries and physical validation. The lab itself calls the process generative design and draws an analogy to evolutionary production of morphology. Its connection to automated discovery is an inference from the documented simulation-guided design search; there is no claim of open-ended evolution or an evolutionary algorithm.
activity: The lab’s September 30, 2026 article reports active projects including a fish-locomotion-inspired soft robot and underactuated hand. Its project page lists multiple 2026 projects. The coral-gripper page reports hundreds of simulated designs and physical validation.

name: Robotics Lab (naXys), Autonomous Systems and Robotics group
institution: University of Namur, Faculty of Computer Science; Namur Institute for Complex Systems (naXys)
summary: The current lab coordinates research in autonomous robotics and models of natural individual and social behavior. Its active BABOTS project develops controllable biological animal robots by reprogramming worms’ or insects’ nervous systems, while the lab’s evolutionary-robotics work studies collective decision and adaptive swarm behavior. The bridge to bio-inspired robotics is explicit in the current group and project pages.
activity: Current naXys page lists BABOTS, coordinated by Tuci and funded through 10/2027, and an ongoing collective-decision project using evolutionary robotics (research-assistant period through 2028). It lists Tuci among current staff.

name: Robotics Lab.@CSE-IIT Guwahati
institution: Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati
summary: Builds networked mobile-robot systems whose distributed agents share information and intelligence using stigmergy and mobile-agent mechanisms, with bio-inspired and artificial-immune learning for embodied cyber-physical systems.
activity: Official lab listing includes 2025 immune-inspired embodied-intelligence and robot-learning publications, current 2026 thesis work on decentralized multi-robot task allocation, and accepted 2026 papers on multi-robot positioning and adaptive skill discovery.

name: Robotics, Evolution and Artificial Life Laboratory (REAL)
lead: Sebastian Risi; Kasper Støy; Payam Zahadat
institution: IT University of Copenhagen
summary: REAL is an AI-rooted lab at ITU Copenhagen combining evolutionary computation, robotics, artificial life, and embodied cognition for adaptive agents.
activity: Current official unit page was opened; the supplied October queue did not provide a dated activity item.

name: Rochefort Research Group — Cortical Information Processing and Energy
institution: University of Edinburgh, Centre for Discovery Brain Sciences
summary: Rochefort’s current projects explicitly investigate how cortical information processing relates to energy consumption. She coauthored the brain energy review with former postdoc Zahid Padamsey.
activity: Current lab research page lists a project on cortical information processing and energy; current team and 2024 research outputs listed.

name: Rodrigo Soto — kinetic theory of active matter programme
institution: Universidad de Chile, Department of Physics
summary: Soto develops statistical-mechanical and kinetic theories for collective organization in active systems, with an explicit current programme that applies those methods to bacteria and embryonic tissues. The work explains emergent biological organization; no Bio-inspired AI system or engineering transfer is claimed.
activity: UChile’s current Physics Department grants list names Soto as PI on a 2026 Fondecyt Regular “Kinetic theory for active matter”; the department describes a four-year theory and simulation project concerning collective behavior in biological systems.

researchPlans.author: Rodrigo Soto

name: Rolandi Group — Bioelectronic Intelligent Control
institution: University of California, Santa Cruz, Baskin School of Engineering
summary: Develops an explicit closed-loop system in which AI estimates wound state and prescribes ion/small-molecule actuation to control tissue healing, and a separate program for bioelectronic control of bacterial membrane voltage/colony communication. This is a direct biological-control/computation bridge.
activity: The current group page describes active DARPA and ARO supported wound-regeneration and bacterial communication programs; the publications page includes recent 2025 work on adaptive machine-learning closed-loop wound therapy.

name: Rosenzweig Lab — experimental evolutionary genomics of major transitions
institution: Georgia Institute of Technology
summary: The lab combines experimental evolutionary genomics with bacteria, yeast, and algae to investigate cell origins, compartmentalization, cooperation, and transitions to multicellularity.
activity: A five-year NASA ICAR project announced in 2023 studies organizing principles of compartmentalization and evolution of novelty/efficiency across scales; the current faculty page describes the active lab and continuing funding.

name: Roy Bar-Ziv Lab — Artificial Cell Systems
institution: Weizmann Institute of Science, Department of Chemical and Biological Physics
summary: The current lab reconstitutes artificial cells from programmed DNA compartments, cell-free gene expression and synthetic genetic oscillators, including communicating cell populations and autonomous assembly of ribosomal subunits. This is direct experimental work on synthetic living organization and protocellular systems under the added life theme; no prebiotic-origin claim is made.
activity: The current Weizmann PI page describes the artificial-cell programme and current self-regenerating protein-synthesis work, citing 2024 and 2025 outputs. The group roster was updated 6 September 2026 and lists the PI and current lab members.

name: Ryan Bahlous-Boldi evolutionary learning research program
institution: Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Computer Science and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory
summary: Current doctoral research program studies how intelligence emerges in adaptive artificial systems that evolve and learn; 2025 QD coauthorship and 2026 diversity-driven policy optimization establish direct continuation.
activity: MIT CSAIL confirms current PhD identity; personal page describes current research on adaptive systems that evolve and learn; 2026 paper on diversity-driven policy optimization has him as first author.

name: Saar Rahav Research Group — Statistical Mechanics of Small Out-of-Equilibrium Systems
institution: Schulich Faculty of Chemistry, Technion – Israel Institute of Technology
summary: The group explicitly studies nonequilibrium thermodynamics of molecular machines and information–thermodynamics relations. This is a specific physical information/energy mechanism covered by Bio theme 4; the current evidence does not describe a biological cell programme or a thermodynamic-learning system, so the fit remains strongly related.
activity: Current group publication list includes recent work on experimental information engines and nonequilibrium thermodynamics; the current homepage states that the group is recruiting graduate researchers.

name: Sabine Hauert Swarm Engineering research programme
institution: University of Bristol, School of Engineering Mathematics and Technology / Bristol Robotics Laboratory
summary: Hauert leads an active Swarm Engineering programme. Its specific 2025 “Ghost Swarms” project uses evolutionary algorithms to infer human-readable controllers for natural and engineered swarms from environmental traces. The exact link to the Bio-inspired evolutionary-robotics theme is explicit for this project; it does not imply that every Swarm Engineering project uses evolutionary algorithms.
activity: Official profile lists an active 2025–2030 Trustworthy Robot Swarms grant, 2026 swarm publications and Alharthi’s swarm-controller-learning thesis project under Hauert; the 2025 paper documents the method.

name: SACRAL / Takashi Ikegami Laboratory
institution: The University of Tokyo
summary: An artificial-life lab studying coupled cognitive systems and embodied recurrent neural systems, with 2025 papers on LLM agents and grounding GPT-4 in a humanoid robot.
activity: 2025 papers including 'From text to motion: grounding GPT-4 in a humanoid robot Alter3' (Frontiers in Robotics and AI, 2025) and 2025 arXiv LLM-agent papers; March 2025 symposium.

teamMembers.role: External Lab. Member / JSPS Research Fellow PD

name: Sahu Lab
institution: University of Texas at Austin, McKetta Department of Chemical Engineering
summary: The group explicitly studies how molecular interactions produce collective behavior in soft and living materials. Current lipid-membrane work combines equilibrium molecular dynamics with continuum theory to quantify membrane rheology and fluctuations. This is mechanistic cellular-scale work on living matter and collective physical behavior; it does not claim an engineered biological-computing application.
activity: The official publication list shows multiple 2026 lipid-membrane studies and 2025 membrane-methods work. A 4 September 2026 paper by Sahu describes equilibrium molecular-dynamics analysis and continuum-theory validation of membrane shear viscosity; the current lab page gives the group identity and research programme.

name: Sakana AI — Frontier Intelligence Group (FIG)
lead: FIG research collective; individual group head not stated
institution: Sakana AI K.K.
summary: FIG explicitly attributes biologically inspired physical cellular-brick work to its members. Local neural cellular automata let modular hardware recognize collective shape and locate damage. Autonomous actuation and full physical self-repair remain prospective, rather than demonstrated capabilities.
activity: The current September 2026 FIG announcement attributes Smart Cellular Bricks to its members; the July 2026 primary method page reports physical hardware shape-recognition experiments.

name: Sakana AI — RSI Lab
lead: Research team; individual lead not verified
institution: Sakana AI
summary: Sakana AI's RSI Lab builds open-ended, adaptive architectures that collectively self-improve, modeled explicitly on open-ended biological evolution.
activity: Page announces the formal establishment of the Sakana AI RSI Lab and describes recent milestones; no explicit dated 2024-2026 output in fetched text.
