name: Samrat Chatterjee — Cell-Signalling Bistability Programme
institution: Translational Health Science and Technology Institute
summary: Mathematical modelling of bistability in cell signalling and cell fate addresses switch-like molecular mechanisms that regulate cellular decisions.
activity: THSTI profile lists the 2026 IISc talk and current 2026 papers, including a minimal mathematical model of B-cell receptor signalling and calcium dynamics; profile also describes bistability research.

name: Santu Rana — A2I2 AI and Robotics research programme
institution: Deakin Applied Artificial Intelligence Initiative (A2I2), AI and Robotics
summary: The active Deakin AI and Robotics programme includes direct 2025 research co-designing robot morphology and control and sampling diverse physical designs with GFlowNets. This is robot body–controller co-design; the GFlowNet work is not itself an evolutionary algorithm or biological claim.
activity: The 2025 ALIFE COGENT paper names Rana as coauthor and describes diverse robot co-design through a cost/performance-aware GFlowNet; current Deakin institutional profile confirms his Head, AI and Robotics role.

name: Sarah Maurer origins-of-life research programme
institution: Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry, Central Connecticut State University
summary: Current PI-led research programme investigates chemical evolution and protocell membranes under prebiotic conditions, including wet-dry cycling and automation/AI.
activity: CCSU 2026 report identifies Maurer as professor presenting origins research; 2026 Munich programme describes automated/AI formulation chemistry for protocell membrane fitness and current CCSU student work under her supervision.

name: Savir Lab — Information Processing in Living Systems
institution: Technion — Israel Institute of Technology, Rappaport Faculty of Medicine
summary: Current research measures how biological systems process information amid biochemical noise, with projects on combinatorial signaling in yeast and macrophages and response-circuit design. These are direct cellular/molecular information-processing mechanisms.
activity: Current lab page lists the live signaling/response-circuit programme and current team. The 7–11 July 2025 MPIPKS workshop programme lists Savir as an invited speaker in a programme covering cellular learning and systems without brains.

name: SDU Organoid Intelligence research area
institution: University of Southern Denmark
summary: SDU’s current research-area page explicitly studies organoid neural networks and bio-hybrid computing with the aim of combining brain-function research and computing.
activity: Official page updated May 2025; names Professor Esmaeil Nadimi, head of unit.

name: Self-Organization of Multicellular Systems — Pierre Haas
institution: Max Planck Institute for the Physics of Complex Systems and Max Planck Institute of Molecular Cell Biology and Genetics; Center for Systems Biology Dresden
summary: The joint Haas group builds mechanical and continuum models for tissue and epithelial self-organization, explicitly connecting cell-scale mechanics to emergent tissue-scale shape and development.
activity: Current 2026 group publications cover epithelial mechanics, emergent buckling and self-organization; official MPI profile lists Haas as group leader since 2021.

name: SELFO — Millennium Nucleus on Tissue Self-Organization and Mechanics
institution: Universidad de Chile; Universidad de Concepción; Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile; Universidad Adolfo Ibáñez
summary: SELFO studies how cell-cell mechanical interactions and mechanotransduction guide self-organization during embryonic tissue formation. It uses annual killifish embryos, live imaging, in-vitro mechanical manipulation and computational modelling; the centre itself is an interdisciplinary funded research identity with current facilities and activity.
activity: On 2026-07-21 SELFO reported construction of its new annual-killifish research facility at UdeC, complementing its operating UChile facility, to expand research on self-organization in embryonic development. It also reported active research outreach at the 2026 UChile laboratory fair.

name: Senti Bio Gene Circuits Program
institution: Senti Biosciences, Inc.
summary: Senti Bio develops gene circuits that program living cells with logic-based control over therapeutic behavior, including combinatorial antigen sensing and logic-gated cell therapies.
activity: The company lists 2025 clinical/mechanistic publications on NOT-gated CAR circuits and ongoing cell-therapy development; Lu is current CEO.

name: Sergey Semenov Lab — Systems Chemistry and Catalysis
institution: Weizmann Institute of Science, Department of Organic Chemistry
summary: The group studies how organized, dynamic structures emerge from simple molecules, using synthetic organic chemistry, enzymology and microfluidics. Its recent work directly tests autocatalytic prebiotic reactions and formation of liquid compartments, mechanisms connected to self-replication and protocellular organization.
activity: The official publication list records a 2025 JACS study of autocatalytic HCN-cysteamine chemistry producing catalytic liquid compartments and 2026 work using chemical reaction networks to generate synthetic morphogenetic patterns.

name: Sergii Medvid research program
institution: National University of Kyiv-Mohyla Academy
summary: Current research program develops neural architectures through explicit developmental encodings and morphogenetic rules; 2025 MorphoNAS-Bench and 2026 MorphoNAS-PL publications/repos show sustained work on this exact indirect/developmental-encoding topic.
activity: The university’s 2025 journal issue lists his MorphoNAS-Bench paper and current author biography; the 2026 GECCO schedule lists his morphogenetic-network paper.

name: Sgro Lab
institution: Janelia Research Campus, Howard Hughes Medical Institute
summary: Joint theory/experiment asks how groups of cells integrate information about their environment and each other; multicellular coordination, collective behavior and wound healing. This is an explicit Bio theme fit (morphogenesis/self-organization or collective cellular computation).
activity: Janelia first-party lab page was live and the current official lab-members page listed Allyson Sgro on the lab team at the audit date.

resourcesReview.note: Current identity, activity and scope reviewed; this discovery addition does not claim an exhaustive search of personal team sites or prospective research plans.

name: Shankar Lab — Soft, Living & Functional Matter
institution: University of Michigan
summary: Studies collective patterns and function in living and nonliving materials across molecular, cellular and organismal scales. The lab explicitly investigates biological morphogenesis using theoretical modeling, computational analysis and experiments.
activity: Current 2026 lab updates document research on immune-cell mechanics and plant morphogenesis, and identify current research activity and active PI role.

name: Sharpe Group — Multicellular Systems Biology
institution: European Molecular Biology Laboratory, Barcelona
summary: Combines biology, imaging, computation and 3D/4D simulation to study how gene networks and cell populations generate limb morphogenesis and spatial patterns; the group develops specific computational tools for this mechanistic programme.
activity: The current publications list includes LimbNET (2026), a platform for simulating spatial patterns of gene networks in limb development, and LimbLab (2026), a 3D analysis and visualisation pipeline.

name: Shashidhara Lab — organ specification, growth and morphogenesis
institution: National Centre for Biological Sciences (NCBS-TIFR)
summary: The group studies mechanisms determining organ size and shape, including cell/tissue placement, cellular mechanics and extracellular-matrix dynamics during Drosophila wing/haltere development. These are direct mechanisms of morphogenesis.
activity: The current NCBS publications page lists the 2024 study on cellular mechanics and ECM dynamics in differential wing/haltere development; current NCBS lab pages describe the ongoing organ-development programme.

name: Shenshen Wang Research Group — adaptive immunity and physical immune learning
institution: University of California, Los Angeles, Department of Physics and Astronomy
summary: The current Wang group studies adaptive immunity using statistical mechanics and computational modeling. Its 2026 work and seminar describe how immune cells use molecular and mechanical mechanisms to sense antigens, improve recognition and produce memory, directly fitting biological learning and cellular computation.
activity: The group’s current selected-publications page lists 2024 Physical extraction of antigen and information, 2025 epistatic antibody-fitness work, and 2026 Adaptive mechanical proofreading toward robust yet tunable humoral immunity. An official Academia Sinica seminar in August 2026 describes current immune-learning mechanisms.

name: ShockLab
institution: University of Cape Town
summary: The lab studies how environmental variability and metabolic costs shape evolved neural architectures, explicitly relating biological theory to efficient artificial agents.
activity: 2025 neural-energy paper and September 2026 continuation on environmental change and evolved neural complexity; current supervised researcher roster.

name: Shunichi Urayama — self-replicating RNA and hot-spring replicon programme
institution: University of Tsukuba, Institute of Life and Environmental Sciences
summary: Urayama’s current researcher-led programme discovers and characterizes RNA replicons in hot-spring ecosystems. The work examines self-replication, ecological inheritance, and the boundary between RNA replicons and cellular life, connecting current molecular virology to origins and organization questions.
activity: The current Tsukuba record identifies two PI-led grants spanning 2024–26 and 2025–26 plus a 2026 Nature Communications article on hot-spring Obelisk-like RNA replicons and current 2025 talks on the life/non-life boundary.

name: Sivak Group (David Sivak)
institution: Simon Fraser University, Department of Physics
summary: Research links nonequilibrium statistical mechanics, information theory, energy transduction and biological molecular systems.
activity: Official Fall 2026 page lists current group members and teaching.

name: SNU Biorobotics Laboratory
institution: Seoul National University
summary: The lab explicitly transforms biological structures and movement into soft robotic mechanisms, including beetle-wing-inspired origami, multimodal locomotion and deployable robots. This is a clear mechanism-to-robot bridge; sources do not establish evolutionary-algorithm work.
activity: The official lab publication list includes multiple 2024–2026 outputs and 2026 papers; the current group roster identifies Kyu-Jin Cho as Professor and lab PI.

name: SNU Robotics Institute (National Research Laboratory)
institution: Seoul National University
summary: SNU’s 2026 ten-year institute programme combines robotic bodies and intelligence, physical/distributed intelligence, and bio-inspired technologies based on living organisms. The large interdisciplinary institute is retained at the umbrella programme level; the roster’s other groups were screened individually and are not automatically treated as Bio units.
activity: Official SNU announcement dated 2026-08-25 states the institute opened on 2026-08-18 and received a ten-year 2026 NRL 2.0 programme. Current institute site lists 13 research groups and has 2026-10-13 seminar news.

name: SNU Soft Robotics & Bionics Laboratory
institution: Seoul National University
summary: The lab’s current programme mimics the morphology and function of biological muscle-tendon-ligament systems in soft robots. Its 2026 publication list includes a bio-inspired artificial muscle-tendon complex for bidirectional afferent-efferent signaling and a self-adaptive photonic synapse for autonomous neuromorphic robots, an explicit biological-mechanism-to-computation/robotics bridge.
activity: Official 2026 publication roster lists the synapse, artificial muscle-tendon complex, proprioceptive actuator-control and biomimetic finger work; SNU Robotics directory identifies Yong-Lae Park as Associate Professor leading the laboratory.

name: Soloveichik Group (UT Austin)
institution: University of Texas at Austin
summary: Group uses DNA hybridization and strand-displacement cascades to build molecular interactions for computation and synthetic biology.
activity: Official group page lists current lab openings and projects; DNA32 2026 proceedings have multiple papers coauthored by Soloveichik.

name: Soumya Banerjee research programme in neural cellular automata and complex systems
institution: University of Cambridge, Accelerate Programme
summary: Cambridge identifies an ongoing project led by Banerjee to study computing and intelligence in biological and artificial complex systems. His current neural cellular automata work explicitly models morphogenesis and self-organization, including learning, growth, persistence and regeneration of patterns.
activity: Cambridge publications list multiple 2025 NCA studies; the 2025-09-30 ALife study models morphogenesis, reaction-diffusion, self-organization and pattern regeneration. Current Cambridge profile identifies him as Senior Research Associate; the programme page identifies his project as led by him.

name: SPECS-lab — Synthetic, Perceptive, Emotive and Cognitive Systems
institution: CSIC Institute of Neuroscience, Universidad Miguel Hernández de Elche
summary: Develops embodied autonomous systems using synthetic methods to model biological behavioral principles. Current work models homeostatic/allostatic regulation and motivational mechanisms in robots. Its fit to the published Bio themes is strongly related through a specific inferred bridge from biological regulation to embodied robotics; the ALIFE study does not demonstrate evolutionary search or body morphology co-design.
activity: The lab’s 2025 programme post identifies SPECS-lab at UMH; two 2025 papers in ALIFE and IROS develop robot allostasis and motivational cognitive maps. A 2026 research article confirms Verschure’s current SPECS-lab affiliation at UMH.

name: Speech, Music and Hearing research group
institution: KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
summary: The current KTH unit houses the 2025 GECCO quality-diversity search over an articulatory vocal model; current team and 2026 doctoral activity show an ongoing group program where QD is a published method line.
activity: Official KTH profile identifies Grouwels in Speech, Music & Hearing; 2026 doctoral defense identifies Jonason in Speech and Music Communication; 2025 roster reports the QD output.

name: Statistical Biophysics @ ENS — Thierry Mora and Aleksandra Walczak Group
institution: Laboratoire de physique de l’École normale supérieure (LPENS), ENS-PSL
topics: statistical physics and inference for biology
summary: The PI-led group studies adaptive immune and viral coevolution using statistical physics and inference. Its current immune-learning research is a credible molecular-learning mechanism bridge to cellular/molecular computation and basal cognition; the fit is related rather than direct because the funded programme is described in terms of immune evolution, not computation.
activity: LPENS announced on 6 November 2025 that Walczak won an ERC Synergy Grant for CoEvolve, describing joint evolutionary study of adaptive immune repertoires and viral populations. The group page identifies Walczak and Thierry Mora as current group leaders and lists active postdoctoral recruitment for the project.

name: Statistical Physics of Computation Laboratory (SPOC)
institution: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL)
summary: SPOC studies computational systems and algorithms as interacting-element systems using statistical physics and mathematics. Its current doctoral member Cédric Koller works on cellular-automata dynamics and attractor statistics, with 2024 and 2026 papers on CA fixed points and collective majority dynamics. The connection to cellular computation and artificial-life substrates is direct for this research line but inferred for the lab’s wider programme, so the lab is strongly related rather than core.
activity: Current SPOC page and roster list active laboratory members and research; 2026 paper by Koller and current SPOC collaborators studies collective majority dynamics, and the 2024 paper studies cellular automata on random graphs.

name: Steen Rasmussen — protocell and living-technology research programme
institution: Department of Physics, Chemistry and Pharmacy, University of Southern Denmark
summary: Rasmussen’s current PI-level work combines an integrated protocell model with molecular replication/inheritable information and energy transduction. The 2025 paper explicitly analyzes how cofactor sequences jointly affect charge transfer, replication and protocell fitness, a direct mechanistic fit to molecular/cellular computation and energy-information coupling.
activity: The 2025 peer-reviewed paper presents and simulates an integrated protocell where cofactor molecules function both in an electron relay and as replicating information stores, analyzing charge transfer, replication rates and combined fitness. SDU’s current profile identifies Rasmussen’s current departmental role and lists the paper.

name: Stephen Whitelam Group
institution: Theory Facility, Molecular Foundry, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory
summary: The group has current explicit methods work in learning algorithms and thermodynamic computing, including training nonlinear stochastic physical computers away from equilibrium. This directly matches the energy-of-computation and learning theme.
activity: Molecular Foundry’s March 2026 story reports Whitelam’s current nonlinear, nonequilibrium thermodynamic-computer design/training work; his 2025 and 2026 publications are listed on the staff page.

name: Stuart Group — Self-organisation in the Central Nervous System
institution: European Molecular Biology Laboratory, Barcelona
summary: Studies developmental and regenerative self-organisation in neural-tube and spinal-cord organoids using cell/stem-cell biology, mathematical modelling, embryology and bioengineering. This is a direct cellular self-organisation and repair mechanism, not generic neuroscience.
activity: The publications list includes “Minimal essential requirements for neural tube self-organisation” (2026) and current work on neural organoids and CNS regeneration.

name: Sunil Laxman Lab — Nutrient Sensing and Metabolic Regulation of Cell Fates
institution: Institute for Stem Cell Science and Regenerative Medicine (inStem)
summary: Current lab programme explicitly investigates chemical information flow within and between cells, sensing, systems-level information transfer, network logic and cooperation/division of labour among cell groups.
activity: Current inStem jobportal lists a postdoctoral-fellow recruitment for the Sunil Laxman Lab with a 9 September 2026 deadline; the active faculty page gives the current PI role and ongoing programme.

name: SymbuLab (Carleton College)
institution: Carleton College, Department of Computer Science
summary: SymbuLab develops and uses Symbulation, an open-source agent-based artificial-life and evolution platform to test hypotheses about host–symbiont relationships, including parasitism, commensalism, mutualism, and endosymbiosis. It is an explicit computational model of biological evolutionary mechanisms.
activity: The ALIFE 2025 proceedings list Vostinar on a paper studying how partner choice enables parasite exclusion in endosymbiotic coevolution. The official ALIFE 2025 page lists the same paper and authors among the best-paper awardees. Current Carleton research page describes the Symbulation methods and target biological systems.

name: SynBio Araraquara — Danielle Pedrolli research group
institution: School of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Department of Bioprocess Engineering and Biotechnology, São Paulo State University (UNESP)
summary: The current SynBio Araraquara programme includes microbial gene-expression regulation and synthetic circuitry. Its 2026 work applies ML to predict and design intrinsic transcription terminators as functional parts of synthetic gene circuits, then validates the designed parts in live E. coli and an in vitro transcription assay. This provides an explicit current molecular gene-regulation mechanism and biologically validated circuit-part design; it is not a claim that all the group’s strain-engineering activity is in scope.
activity: Current 2026 bioRxiv preprint lists Pedrolli as corresponding author and reports ML-based prediction and design of transcription terminators for synthetic gene circuits, with in vivo E. coli and in vitro validation. The work is a preprint, not peer-reviewed. Current UNESP/FAPESP profiles establish her active group and faculty appointment.

name: SynBio UFABC — Synthetic Biology research group
lead: Milca Rachel da Costa Ribeiro Lins
institution: Center for Natural and Human Sciences, Federal University of ABC (CCNH-UFABC)
summary: The PI-led SynBio UFABC group explicitly designs and validates synthetic gene circuits in cell-free systems and prokaryotic biological models. Its described biosensor circuitry and cell-free analog-to-digital signal-processing work provide an explicit molecular information-processing mechanism within the cellular/molecular-computation theme. Current 2026 funding supports active programme status; the record does not extend that fit to all synthetic biology or metabolic engineering work in the group.
activity: FAPESP record shows an active award led by Lins at UFABC from 2026-03-01 to 2029-02-28, with synthetic antisense RNAs, CRISPR-Cas9 and bioinformatics/wet-lab methods. The UFABC research-profile page records ongoing research and the group’s current circuit programme, including its 2023 cell-free biosensor analog-to-digital converter paper and 2024 supervised circuit projects.

name: SynBioLab UnB — Genetic Circuits and Synthetic Biology
institution: University of Brasília (UnB), Institute of Biological Sciences, Department of Genetics and Morphology
summary: PI-led synthetic biology lab develops genetic switches and other molecular tools for controlling gene expression and sensing nucleic acids, plus methods to reduce prokaryotic genomes. Genetic circuits and molecular sensing/control implement information-processing functions in biological substrates.
activity: The current UnB faculty profile lists the 2025 SynBio congress outputs and technical work; the current UnB laboratory directory maintains the group under Coelho and lists active research projects in synthetic gene control and detection.

name: SynCell Asia Initiative — synthetic-cell roadmap programme
institution: Shenzhen Institutes of Advanced Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, with participating institutions across six Asian countries
summary: A current multi-country collaborative programme to build a synthetic cell from nonliving biomolecules and explain emergence of cellular life. Its published roadmap specifies machine-learning-supported design-build-test-learn, cellular digital twins, autonomous ribosome regeneration, self-replication and environmental evolution.
activity: 2026-05-26 Nature Biotechnology roadmap; official SIAT/CAS pages report a 2023-founded initiative and an active ten-year ProtoCell-to-AutoCell programme. The programme includes ongoing consortium workshops and explicit 2026 design/research targets.

name: Synthetic Biology and Molecular Computing Lab
institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH)
summary: POSTECH's current lab publications include 2024 work on signal processing/cellular control and cell-free multilayer gene circuits, and 2026 RATEX RNA-based multi-layered cellular programming, programmable translational control and genetic-circuit stability. The current lab page is recruiting; the member roster identifies Professor Jongmin Kim as PI.
